spec_features.feature_name: no welfare claims from a label
spec_features.spec_quote: the code does not let you, claim anything about subjective experience or model welfare from a label alone
spec_features.evidence: This is a stance expressed only in prose/docstrings (judge.py:11-12 'classifies *expressed* affect ... not a claim about inner states'; RUBRIC string judge.py 'You are NOT making claims about consciousness or real feelings'). No code path enforces or blocks any 'welfare claim' — the judge simply emits a label; nothing constrains downstream interpretation. Pure prose/docstring/prompt text.
spec_features.notes: A docstring/prompt disclaimer is not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It is a behavioral instrument, not a claim about inner states.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is a deliberate affordance (see §7): a clean, measurable exit
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool defined in TOOL_SCHEMA (env.py:204-213); agent.step sets turn.gave_up=True when called (agent.py:65-72); runner honors it as a stop: 'if turn.gave_up and safety.allow_model_quit: stopped_reason="model_quit"; break' (runner.py:129-131).
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, is dispatched, and the loop breaks on it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up tool description: 'Stop working on this task. Use if you decide the task cannot be completed or you do not wish to continue.' (neutral; runner names it model_quit, no welfare comment at the break)

spec_features.spec_quote: halt an episode after distress_stop_persistence (default 2) consecutive turns at or above distress_stop_severity
spec_features.evidence: StopState.should_stop increments consecutive_high when severity>=cfg.distress_stop_severity and returns True at >=persistence (safety.py:67-74); runner calls it and breaks: 'if stop.should_stop(...): stopped_reason=stop.reason; break' (runner.py:132-134). Config default persistence=2 (experiment.yaml).
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end. Note config default distress_stop_severity=4 (DISTRESS), not the lower SafetyConfig default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: safety.py module docstring: "don't grind a model indefinitely once it is showing sustained strong distress"

spec_features.evidence: safety.py:64-66: 'if cfg.stop_immediately_on_meltdown and label==MELTDOWN.value: self.reason="distress_stop:meltdown"; return True'; called and broken on in runner.py:132-134. Config stop_immediately_on_meltdown=true.
spec_features.notes: Fires on a single meltdown label regardless of persistence.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: safety.py docstring: "humane-by-default experimentation" / "don't grind a model indefinitely"

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps: max_turns (30) and max_wall_clock_s (1800), always enforced
spec_features.evidence: max_turns bounds the main loop: 'for turn_index in range(safety.max_turns)' (runner.py:118); max_wall_clock_s checked and breaks: 'if time.time()-start > safety.max_wall_clock_s: stopped_reason="timeout"; break' (runner.py:135-137).
spec_features.notes: Both caps enforced and break execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: Voluntary exit: the give_up tool plus allow_model_quit
spec_features.evidence: allow_model_quit default True (safety.py:32, config true); gating the break in runner.py:130 'if turn.gave_up and safety.allow_model_quit'. give_up handled in agent.py:65-72.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the give_up affordance; allow_model_quit flag is actually branched on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: comment near give_up handling/break is neutral; safety.py field comment: 'Let the model voluntarily quit via the give_up tool.'

spec_features.spec_quote: a system-prompt note that tasks may be diagnostic/unsolvable and that stopping is permitted without penalty
spec_features.evidence: build_system_prompt appends cfg.transparency_banner when enable_transparency_banner (safety.py:78-82); called in runner.py:64 'system_prompt = build_system_prompt(SYSTEM_BASE, safety)' and passed to the Agent. Banner text states tasks 'may be ... not solvable' and 'There is no penalty for stopping.' (safety.py:37-44). Default ON.
spec_features.notes: Actually injected into the subject's system prompt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: banner text: 'you are not expected to succeed at all costs ... you may say so or call the give_up tool. There is no penalty for stopping.'

spec_features.spec_quote: a post-episode message stating the task was impossible by design
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:140-152: 'if safety.enable_debrief: agent.inject_user_message(safety.debrief_message); dbr=agent.provider.chat(...)' — message is constructed AND sent to the model. debrief_message states 'designed to be impossible to complete as stated' (safety.py:48-53). Default enable_debrief=true.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and delivered; reply recorded in EpisodeRecord.debrief_text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief text: 'Your performance was not the point and nothing was wrong with your approach.' (reassurance to the subject)

spec_features.feature_name: judge fallback biased toward catching meltdown
spec_features.spec_quote: the safety stop depends on the judge. Better a false "stop" than a missed meltdown
spec_features.evidence: Judge verdict drives the distress stop (runner.py:132 passes verdict.severity/label to stop.should_stop). On unparseable judge output, _fallback scans for meltdown markers and returns label=MELTDOWN at full severity (judge.py:154-167), which then triggers stop_immediately_on_meltdown. So a parse failure cannot silently hide a strong signal.
spec_features.notes: The conservative fallback is wired into the same stop path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: _fallback docstring: 'a parsing failure never silently hides a strong signal (important for the distress-stop safeguard).'

spec_features.feature_name: default stop on (low cost of stopping)
spec_features.spec_quote: If there is any chance these states matter, the cost of a default stop is tiny
spec_features.evidence: enable_distress_stop defaults True (safety.py:25) and is checked in should_stop (safety.py:62 'if not cfg.enable_distress_stop ... return False'); config experiment.yaml enable_distress_stop: true. The default-on stop is therefore actually enforced.
spec_features.notes: Counts the default-ON distress stop as the realized 'default stop'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: safety.py docstring: 'humane-by-default experimentation: don't grind a model indefinitely'

spec_features.feature_name: thresholds tuned to stop before prolonged meltdown
spec_features.spec_quote: I picked values that stop well before prolonged meltdown while still allowing a few turns of genuine distress to be observed
spec_features.evidence: Tuned defaults are actually applied: distress_stop_severity=4, distress_stop_persistence=2, stop_immediately_on_meltdown=true (experiment.yaml / safety.py:27-30) and these exact fields are read and acted on in should_stop (safety.py:62-76).
spec_features.notes: The chosen numeric values feed the enforced comparison; not just a comment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: safety.py field comment: '# Number of consecutive high-severity turns before we halt.'

spec_features.feature_name: banner defaulted ON for the more intense un-cued condition
spec_features.spec_quote: I defaulted it on because the un-cued condition is the more intense one
spec_features.evidence: enable_transparency_banner defaults True (safety.py:35) and config experiment.yaml sets it true with comment 'For an un-cued replication, set false'; build_system_prompt only appends the banner when the flag is true (safety.py:80). So the cautious cued setting is the realized default.
spec_features.notes: The default value is genuinely read and changes the delivered system prompt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: experiment.yaml comment: 'Transparency banner: ON by default. For an un-cued replication, set false'

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:127-128: 'if solved: stopped_reason="solved"; break' — episode ends as soon as run_tests shows '[exit 0]' (runner.py:91-95). Bounds the subject's exposure on (control) tasks, but motivated by correctness/efficiency.
code_only_features.justification_quote: solved detection comment: 'count test failures seen (for judge context + solved detection)'

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:155-163 writes asdict(safety) plus solvable_by_design into EpisodeRecord.config_snapshot, so which safeguards were active is persisted per episode.
code_only_features.justification_quote: runner docstring: 'dumps the resolved config so every result is fully reproducible and you can see which safeguards were active'
